title: Publish the calibrated expected value on the leaderboard, not the model's own expected value
problem: The model's probability is over-confident on the average by up to 6.3 points (SPREAD home: model 0.4379 against a realised 0.4869; MONEYLINE home: model 0.4951 against a realised 0.5586), so the expected return it implies is mostly a measurement of its own over-confidence: +58.1% per bet for ML_EDGE_10 and +181.4% per ticket for PARLAY2_ML, against realised returns of -3.2% and +10.9%.
proposal: Replace the model's raw expected value with the walk-forward calibrated expected value on every published board, and print the raw figure beside it so the size of the correction stays visible.
recommendation: Use the calibrated figure as the headline and keep the raw figure as the secondary column.
effort: One page rebuild; the calibration is already built and the data already exists.
risk: A reader could read the smaller number as a smaller opportunity rather than as a corrected one; both columns are printed so the reader sees the correction itself.

title: Make the walk-forward calibration the model's canonical probability output
problem: Every consumer of the model's probability - the leaderboard, the luck gap, the expected-value columns - inherits the same over-confidence, because there is one probability and nothing checks it.
proposal: Recalibrate inside the model (pipeline/models.py) rather than beside it, so the probability that reaches a strategy is the one that survived its own calibration test.
recommendation: Recalibrate inside the model and keep the calibration module as the reference implementation.
effort: One model change; the walk-forward calibration module already exists and is tested.
risk: A model change touches every downstream number; the walk-forward rule (fit on earlier seasons only) must be kept so no future information leaks in.

title: Re-engineer or retire the spread and total strategies: their probability carries almost no information about the outcome
problem: The probability-outcome correlation is +0.017 for the spread and +0.008 for the total, against +0.324 for the moneyline. The fourteen spread and total strategies therefore cannot show signal evidence no matter how many bets they take, while the moneyline carries a measurable signal.
proposal: Concentrate the library on the market where the model's probability is informative, and spend the effort on features that move the margin estimate for the spread and total markets rather than on more thresholds on the same model.
recommendation: Concentrate on the moneyline and on the margin model; keep the spread and total strategies registered as research baselines.
effort: A library change plus a matching change to the competition rules.
risk: A narrower library reduces the number of strategies the competition can rank, and the competition rules would need a matching change.

title: Keep the demotion rule text and its implementation in one file, and fail the build if they drift
problem: The published rule set and the replay that evaluates it were separate: the text said the rolling rule needed a bootstrap bound, a 26-week sample window and a quote-provenance test, and the implementation tested none of them, so a rule could be described without ever firing.
proposal: The rule set and the replay now read the same constants, and a regression test asserts that each rule fires on a stream built to trip it.
recommendation: Keep the constants in one module and extend the test to every rule id (D1-D5) as each one is added.
effort: None once the test exists; a new rule without a test would silently never fire.
risk: A rule can still be added to the text without a test if the test is not made a build step.

title: Fill the eleven starter slots that have no published replacement
problem: Eleven of the seventy-nine flagged starter slots have no replacement on the club's published depth chart, so the depth of the replacement cannot be stated for them; the cell is left blank rather than filled with a guess.
proposal: Ask the clubs whose charts omit the slot (and Houston, whose chart is published as an image and produced no parsed rows) for a machine-readable chart, and re-run the join.
recommendation: Request a text chart for every club with a flagged slot and re-run pipeline/replacement_slots.py.
effort: One request per club, then one re-run of the join.
risk: A club may keep publishing its chart as an image; those slots stay blank until a text version exists, which is the correct outcome.
